'''Tanoe Shrine''' (田乃家神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha (auxiliary shrine)}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (Naikū) within {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. This article also covers the '''Tanoe-Mimae Shrine''' (田乃家御前神社), which shares the same precinct as Tanoe Shrine.

Both shrines enshrine deities that serve as {{ill|guardian deities|ja|守護神}} of {{ill|Farmer|en|Farmer|qid=Q131512|lt=farmhouses}}<ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): page 69</ref>.

== Overview ==

This section describes common information about both shrines.

Located at {{ill|Tamaki, Mie|en|Tamaki, Mie|qid=Q587348|lt=Tamaki}}, [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Watarai District]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Yano Aza Miyamae 387<ref name="sk1">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 211</ref>. There is a theory that the Yano area, where the shrine is situated, is the final resting place of {{ill|Princess Wakatarashihime|ja|稚足姫皇女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Princess Wakatara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55533316}}, who served as a {{ill|Saiō|en|Saiō|qid=Q19841349|lt=Saio}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.town.meiwa.mie.jp/romantic/saio/saio4.html|title=Sites Associated with the Saio (Outside of Town) - Meiwa Town Office|publisher=Meiwa Town, Mie Prefecture|language=Japanese|accessdate=2013-11-03|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1103-2045-21/www.town.meiwa.mie.jp/romantic/saio/saio4.html|archivedate=2013-11-03}}</ref>. 

According to the "Chūnansei Development Area Archaeological Map," there are four {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} (ancient Kofuns) within the precincts<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 61</ref>, but field research by Masafumi Kimoto confirmed five<ref name="sk1"/>. Many {{ill|Archaeological site|en|Archaeological site|qid=Q839954|lt=archaeological sites}} from the {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|qid=Q207858|lt=Yayoi period}} and {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} have been discovered in the Yano area<ref name="sk1"/>. Additionally, within the precincts are the "Prohibited Killing Stone" established by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kishu Domain}} in {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|qid=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō}} 9 (1724) and a water basin dated {{ill|Tenpō|en|Tenpō|qid=Q1369045|lt=Tenpō}} 13 (1842)<ref name="sg">{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area04/03.html?iframe=true&width=1000&height=700|title=Tanoya Gozen Shrine - 125 Shrines｜Sengukan|publisher=Sengukan|language=Japanese|accessdate=2013-11-03|archiveurl=https://megalodon.jp/2013-1103-2159-39/www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area04/03.html?iframe=true&width=1000&height=700|archivedate=2013-11-03}}</ref>.

The two shrines share the same precinct and have a single {{ill|Shinto architecture|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shrine building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=shinmei-zukuri}} architectural style with a wooden shingle roof, facing south and enclosed by a single layer of {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} (sacred fence)<ref name="sk1"/>. There is one {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shinmei torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk1"/>. No {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/offertory box|qid=Q135491444}} is present. The shrine grounds cover an area of 13,114 m²<ref name="sk1"/>.

== Tanoya Shrine ==

Tanoya Shrine Ranks 5th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}<ref name="uy0">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>. It holds a high status among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 65</ref>. Its {{ill|Shintai|en|Shintai|qid=Q327532|lt=Shintai}} is a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|qid=Q35197|lt=mirror}}<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 59</ref>.

The {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|lt=Enshrined deity}} is Ōkami Misamukawa-no-Kami (大神御滄川神)<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. The deity is revered as the guardian of {{ill|Farming|ja|農耕|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/farmers|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24886094}} and {{ill|Dwelling|en|Dwelling|qid=Q699405|lt=households}}<ref name="ic"/>. The prefix "Ōkami" signifies the extension of the divine virtues of {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, the main deity of the Inner Shrine, to this region<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>.

The shrine name "Tanoya" has several theories regarding its origin: one suggests it means "on the rice field" (田の上), another links it to the place name "Tanabe" (田邊郷), and a third relates it to "Tato" (田戸), referring to rice fields and residences near government-owned paddies<ref name="sk8">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 208</ref>.

== Tanoya Gozen Shrine ==

Tanoya Gozen Shrine Ranks 6th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine<ref name="uy0"/>. Its main hall no longer exists, and the deity is now enshrined together with Tanoya Shrine<ref name="uy1">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 10</ref>.

The enshrined deity is Gozen-no-Kami (御前神)<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/>. Like Ōkami Misamukawa-no-Kami, this deity is also a guardian of farmers<ref name="gk"/>.

== History ==

According to the {{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|ja|皇大神宮儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū Ritual Records|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延暦儀式帳|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109596938}}, the shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ar|الإمبراطور يورياكو|arz|الامبراطور يورياكو|azb|یوریاکو (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Júrjaku|de|Yūryaku|es|Yūryaku Tennō|fa|امپراتور یوریاکو|fr|Yūryaku|hr|Yūryaku|id|Kaisar Yūryaku|it|Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇|ka|იურიაკუ|ko|유랴쿠 천황|mr|युराकु|nl|Yuryaku|pl|Yūryaku|pt|Yuryaku|ru|Император Юряку|sh|Car Yūryaku|simple|Emperor Yūryaku|sl|Cesar Jurjaku|sv|Yuryaku|th|จักรพรรดิยูเรียกุ|tl|Emperador Yūryaku|tr|Yūryaku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Юряку|uz|Imperator Yūryaku|vi|Thiên hoàng Yūryaku|yo|Emperor Yūryaku|zh|雄略天皇|zh_min_nan|Yûryaku Thian-hông|zh_yue|雄略天皇|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 68</ref>. Based on the definition of Ise Jingū's auxiliary shrines, it was established before the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, i.e., before {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927)<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref>.

In ancient times, Tanoya Shrine was subject to the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|式年遷宮|lt=Shikinen Sengū}}, rebuilt every 20 years, just like the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk9"/>. However, after an order to rebuild the shrine in {{ill|Ryakuō|en|Ryakuō|qid=Q1146182|lt=Ryakuō}} 3 (1340), no further records of reconstruction exist, and both the rituals and the shrine site fell into obscurity<ref name="sk0"/>.

The shrine was restored on {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun}} 3, 8th day of the 9th month (October 8, 1663, Gregorian calendar) by {{ill|Kiyonaga Kawabe|ja|河辺精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92924151}} (Ōnakatomi Masanaga)<ref name="sk0"/>.

== Rituals ==

Shinto rituals are held in front of the shrine during major festivals such as the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}} (February), {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (June, December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (October), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (November)<ref name="sk0"/>.

** Approximately 40 minutes on foot from {{ill|Tokida Station|eo|Stacio Tokida|ja|外城田駅|jv|Setatsiyun Tokida|ko|도키다역|ur|ٹوکیڈا اسٹیشن|zh|外城田站|qid=Q7813584|lt=Sotoida Station}} (~3.2 km).
